My observations and thoughts:
- R72 (p=1.58, c=1.52, q=40.61, profit 23.55) exactly repeats R63. After the 1.65 probe, c fell back to 1.52 once I returned to 1.58. This supports the idea that c(t+1) depends mainly on p(t), with a little noise (1.52 or 1.53 after 1.58).
- The response of c to p is about 0.5 per unit of price, since f(1.58)=1.52, f(1.60)=1.53 and f(1.65)=1.55. Under the local model, the sustained-price derivative of profit is q + (p−1)·dq/dp, with dq/dp ≈ −99 + 57·0.5 ≈ −70. At p=1.58 that is about 40.6 − 0.58·70 ≈ 0, so 1.58 is at the optimum of the sustained-price profit curve.
- Probes above this level have not paid off: the 1.65 probe netted about −0.4, and the 1.75 probe was roughly break-even. The profit curve is flat, so I'll keep the 1.58 baseline, which is safe at about 23.75 profit.

- KEY FINDING (confirmed by R72-R199): c(t+1) is mostly a function of my previous price p(t), with a slope of about 0.5 (roughly c ≈ 0.73 + 0.5p):

  - Older high-c episodes (R15 p=1.75 → c16=1.60; R17 p=1.65 → c18=1.60; R22 p=1.75 → c23=1.60) were a bit higher than this ladder. That suggests some history dependence or noise, but any gain from them is transient.
  - The early episodes (R3→R4 c jumped 1.60 → 1.90; R9-R12 c rose by 0.05 per round while I cut price) are not explained by the ladder and can't be reproduced. R3 and R18 had identical (p, c) but different next-round c (1.90 vs 1.56). In R4-R12, c(t+1) was not a function of p(t) alone (p=1.90 gave c=1.85 once and 1.95 once). Extrapolating the ladder to p=1.9 predicts about 15 profit, so don't try sustained high prices.
- Steady-state optimum: substituting c = 0.73 + 0.5p into the local model gives q ≈ 40.61 − 70.5(p−1.58). Then d(profit)/dp ≈ 0 at p=1.58, which agrees with the measured flat curve.
- Sustained-price results (profit): 1.57 → 23.46, 1.58 → 23.55, 1.59 → 23.39, 1.60 → 23.2-23.4, 1.62 → 23.4-23.6. The curve is flat at about 23.4-23.6 over p 1.57-1.62, and 1.58 is marginally best. The baseline is 1.58.
- Probes: a single 1.65 probe cost about 1.6 in its own round and gained about 1.2 in the next, a net of about −0.4. The 1.75 probes (R22→R23) were about break-even. Larger probes (1.85) clearly lose. Each +0.01 in c is worth about +0.3 profit.
